# Orbit feature checklist

<!-- Generated by `node scripts/features.mjs` from the behaviour spec, the tests and docs/feature-status.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every row is one behaviour from the clean-room spec. Status per ID: **spec’d** (every row) → **built** → **tested** (a unit or e2e test names the ID) → **feels right** (lead sign-off after a hands-on review against `feel.md`).

**Totals:** 475 spec’d · 167 built (68 partial) · 241 tested · 0 feel right. 10 more are out of scope and not counted.

| P0 | 174 | 110 | 136 |
| P1 | 221 | 50 | 94 |

P0 = milestone-1 core experience, P1 = parity, P2 = later.

| MD-03 | The floating player's look and placement | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | frameless, always-on-top window, 320x180 for 16:9 (keeps the video's shape), bottom-right 16 px inside the work area; rounded corners (a window shape where the system has none) and shadow; video only until hovered, then controls over a dark gradient; the same player on every platform |

| MD-05 | Keyboard and media keys for the floating player | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e | – | with the player focused (clicked) Space plays/pauses and arrows seek 5 s (tested); hardware media keys go through Chromium's media key handling to the playing page, not verifiable under Xvfb |
| MD-06 | Move, resize and zoom the floating player | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | drag or two-finger hover-scroll moves it and it glides to the corner the release or fling heads for; corner drag resizes keeping the shape, at least 200 px wide (tall videos too) and at most half the screen width and the screen's height, with rubber-band resistance; Cmd/Ctrl+scroll or pinch zooms (crops) inside the window; corner and size remembered; doesn't yet move aside for Orbit's alerts and dialogs |
| MD-07 | Ending picture-in-picture | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | returning (select, double-click, Back to tab) ends it with the video playing in the page; x closes it and the media keeps playing in the sidebar controls; closing or unloading the tab stops media and player; navigating the tab or the video ending closes it, without replay |

## Archive, recently closed, history and sidebar backups (prefix AR)

Spec: `spec/archive.md`

| ID | Feature | P | Built | Tested | Feels right | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AR-01 | What goes into the Archive | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | close, auto-archive, Clear, archive-below, pinned/folder/Space delete, Mini Window and Peek pages; entries carry tab, Space name, section, reason; back/forward history kept outside OrbitState (userData/archive, page state in memory only); private and empty tabs never archived; state keeps the newest ~200-300, the rest lives in the Archive store |
| AR-02 | Where the Archive lives and how to open it | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | Library view over the page area (its own view above the tabs, below the command bar and Peek) from the bottom-bar button, ⌘⇧L (Open Library), ⌘T View Archive / Open Library and the macOS Archive menu; reopens to the last section; Esc, ⌘W or selecting another tab closes it and the page gets the keys back; section registry (*.library-section.tsx) for other lanes |
| AR-03 | Archive list layout | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | newest first under Today / Yesterday / date headings; favicon, title, host, time and origin-Space badge; filters by source (all, sidebar, Mini Window), Space and how it closed; per profile (PR-05); virtualised and paged, fast at 10k entries. A row click previews (AR-06); ⌘-click and ⇧-click select |
| AR-04 | Search the Archive | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | search field filters on each keystroke (title and URL, case-insensitive, partial words, every word) using the Archive store's keys (history queryTerms/urlKeyOf); typing on narrows the last answer; Enter restores and shows the top or highlighted match; ⌘F focuses it. The command bar's Archived results search the whole Archive store of the profile, not only the recent entries kept in state |
| AR-05 | Restore an archived tab | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Restore (hover button, Enter, row menu, several selected) puts tabs at the top of their Space's Today in order, with their tab id and back/forward history when the profile matches (never across profiles); routing rule > origin Space > current Space; toast with Go to Space when it lands elsewhere; command bar restores without a jump. A row click previews (AR-06) instead of restoring. Undoing Delete Folder after the Space changed profile also follows the new profile (W3) |
| AR-06 | Preview an archived item without restoring | P2 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | a row click opens its page in a Peek over the Library (the Peek component, its open and close motion); the entry stays archived. ⌘W and Esc close only the Peek and the Library takes the keys back (Enter then restores that row); Open as Tab (⌘O) opens it as a tab and keeps the entry; closing a preview, or a reopen of it, archives no second entry. Missing: a Restore button in the Peek card (peek lane). The Peek carries overlay.archiveEntry and archive.restorePreview restores and closes it. With no tab to preview over (an empty Space), a click opens the page in a new tab |
| AR-07 | Clear the Archive | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Clear Archive… from the Archive entry’s right-click menu in the Library, Archive → Clear Archive… (macOS app menu) and the command bar; always asks in the Library first (Cancel has the focus, Esc cancels), says it can’t be undone and that browsing history is kept; clears the profile shown, and the cleared pages leave the disk at once (the log is rewritten). Delete (a row’s menu, or Delete for the selected rows) shows a toast whose Undo puts the entries back with their history for a minute |
| AR-08 | Retention of archived entries | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | settings.archiveKeepDays, default 30; 30 Days / 90 Days / 1 Year / Forever from the Archive entry’s menu in the Library and Archive → Keep Archived Tabs For (macOS) until Settings exist. A shorter time that would delete entries asks first, in the Library, saying how many (Cancel keeps them all and the time as it was). Purged once the Archive is read at launch, hourly, and at once when a shorter time is confirmed; browsing history is not touched |
| AR-09 | Reopen recently closed tabs | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | ⌘⇧T and ⌘Z walk back through closes with full history (TB-07, TB-18); ⌘Z also shows the tab again when it was the one shown; a closed Peek comes back through the same key (PK-10, peek lane). A page closed in the last 10 minutes keeps its history rank in the command bar (as the archived row). macOS File menu: Reopen Closed Tab and a Recently Closed submenu of the last 10; on every platform the Archive toolbar has a Recently Closed menu. Neither list shows a tab of a private or deleted profile |
| AR-10 | Browsing history view | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | History stays a Library section until Orbit has internal pages (D39), not a page in a tab. ⌘Y (Ctrl+H), Archive → View History (macOS) and the command bar open it next to the Archive: every visit of the current profile from the history store, newest first by day, virtualised and paged, with search (all words, title or address). A row opens its page in a new tab (⌘-click or middle-click: behind the Library); its × or its menu (Open in New Tab, Open in Background, Copy Link, Remove from History) removes every visit to the page. Clearing the Archive leaves it alone |
| AR-11 | Sidebar backups and "Restore Data" | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Backups of the whole sidebar (Spaces, each profile’s Favorites, pinned and Today tabs, folders, split views; no private profiles) in userData/backups, one JSON file each: taken within 5 minutes of a sidebar change (only when it differs from the newest; browsing alone never makes one), once 30 s after launch, before every restore, and with Back Up Now. Kept: the newest 10 of today, then the newest of each of the 10 days before, of each week of the month before that and of each 30 days of the year before that; a deleted profile’s Favorites, Spaces and tabs are taken out of every backup. Help → Restore Data… (macOS) and the command bar open the Backups section of the Library: a dated list (day headings, time, Spaces and tabs; a file that can’t be read is listed as such, without Restore); Restore… asks first, then puts the sidebar back: tabs in both keep their page, tabs only in the backup come back asleep (with the page and history the Archive kept for them, leaving the Archive), tabs opened since go to the Archive, Spaces added since go; private windows and their tabs are left alone; Favorites over 12 go to Today (D33). When the sidebar can’t be backed up first, nothing changes. Each restore is one step on the sidebar’s undo stack (TB-18): the toast’s Undo or ⌘Z, also in the Library, puts back the sidebar it replaced, a second ⌘Z goes further back and ⌘⇧Z restores again; earlier steps stay. After an undo, a window moved off a removed Space stays where it went, and the pages come back asleep |

## Developer tools and Developer mode

Spec: `spec/devtools.md`

| ID | Feature | P | Built | Tested | Feels right | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DT-01 | Open / close DevTools | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | ⌥⌘I / F12 (Ctrl+Shift+I / F12) open DevTools for the selected tab or focused split pane, docked inside its view, and close them, also from inside DevTools; a Peek's or Mini Window's page gets its own. ⌥⌘J (Ctrl+Shift+J) opens them on the Console; View → Developer menu (macOS) and the command bar. A key held down acts once. Copy, paste (after DevTools' own paste warning) and the device toolbar work; links DevTools open become tabs. Windows/Linux: while DevTools have the keyboard, only the DevTools keys reach Orbit |
| DT-02 | Inspect element (context menu and picker) | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | right-click → Inspect (last item) opens DevTools with that element selected, or just selects it when they're open. Picker: ⌥⌘C on macOS, no default key on Windows/Linux, Inspect Element in the command bar. ⇧⌘C stays Copy URL; inside DevTools it is DevTools' own picker. Remap: give the devtools.inspect action ⇧⌘C (and take it from tab.copyUrl) in src/shared/actions.ts, or in Settings → Shortcuts once remapping (ST-08) lands |
| DT-03 | DevTools docking, size and focus | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | docked right/left/bottom or undocked from DevTools' dock menu; the engine keeps the side per profile across restarts. Each tab (pane, Peek, Mini Window) has its own DevTools, shown and hidden with its page; a page shown again takes the docked size last chosen. Undocked: the open key brings them to the front (checked on Linux; macOS unverified), and closes them when they have the keyboard. No windows added, however many tabs have DevTools |
| DT-04 | View page source | P1 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-05 | Developer mode turns on automatically for local development URLs | P1 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-06 | Turn Developer mode on/off for any site | P1 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-07 | Developer mode appearance and toolbar | P1 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-08 | JSON viewer in Developer mode | P2 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-09 | Showcase screenshot | P2 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-10 | Show full URL outside Developer mode | P1 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-11 | Task manager (per-tab memory/CPU) | P1 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-12 | Record a performance trace (local) | P2 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-13 | Internal pages for engine-level settings | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | orbit://<page>/ opens as a normal tab when typed in the command bar or address field, or from another internal page's link; orbit://pages/ lists them; orbit://version/ shows the versions of Orbit, Electron, Chromium, V8, Node and the OS. They follow the app's state (light/dark) through the same bridge as Orbit's UI. A web page can't navigate, frame, redirect to, open, load or fetch them, and gets no bridge. Infrastructure documented for reuse (D39) in src/main/devtools/internal-pages.ts and src/renderer/src/internal/registry.ts: a page is a *.internal-page.tsx module. Missing: the pages owned by other lanes (extensions EX-07, site settings OT-07, passwords OT-11, privacy and clearing data ST-12, languages ST-14, system options ST-12, about UP-07, history AR-10) |
| DT-14 | Hard reload and cache-bypassing reload | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | ⇧⌘R (Ctrl+Shift+R) is the navigation lane's nav.hardReload: page and subresources refetched (no-cache). A crashed page hands the keyboard to the window, so ⇧⌘R brings it back. Stopping a load (Esc, the reload button) is NV-04, the navigation lane's |

## Downloads and the Library

Spec: `spec/downloads.md`

| ID | Feature | P | Built | Tested | Feels right | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DL-01 | Downloading a file (baseline) | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | per-profile sessions save to the profile's folder (OS Downloads), name (1) on collisions, .crdownload until done; a blank tab opened for a download closes; outlives its page; quitting asks while downloads run |
| DL-02 | Download start animation | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | a file icon flies from the page's edge into the Library button (≈0.5 s curved path, ease-out) and the button bounces; one flight per download; reduce motion: a fade on the button. Sidebar hidden: a "Downloading <file>" toast (and "Downloaded"/"Couldn't download"). A Mini Window's downloads show in its main window |
| DL-03 | In-progress indicator at the bottom of the sidebar | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | row above the bottom bar: name truncated in the middle, progress bar, bytes of total, time left (smoothed), ✕ cancels and deletes the partial file; several: newest + "+N", hover or "+N" lists each with its own ✕; done for 4 s, click opens; failed: Resume or Retry, ✕ dismisses; no downloads, no room taken. Right-click: the download's menu |
| DL-04 | Open a finished download, or show it in its folder | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Open (PDF, images, text, audio, video in an Orbit tab; else the system app), Show in Finder / Show in Folder, Copy File (pastes as the file in file managers), Copy Download Link, Remove from List, Delete File; a moved file shows "File Missing" and Download Again. The same menu on the sidebar row, the Library's Downloads rows (right-click or ⋯), the recent-files popover and the flyout. Missing: Open with… (no cross-platform API to list apps) |
| DL-05 | Recent files on hover over the Library icon | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | hovering the Library button 300 ms shows a popover above it, inside the sidebar: the 8 newest downloads (and OS screenshots when chosen), each with its picture or kind icon, name, size and age; a click opens one, dragging drops the file (DL-06), right-click shows its menu; it goes 200 ms after the pointer leaves. Right-click the button: Recent Files with Downloads and Screenshots checkboxes (Downloads on, Screenshots off at first) and Show Screenshots in Library (DL-11). No Captures choice: Orbit has no capture tool (OT-03) |
| DL-06 | Drag a download out (and into web pages) | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e | – | every download drags out as the real file (the OS drag, with a file icon): the sidebar row, the recent-files popover, the Library's Downloads rows and Media tiles, and the Ctrl+J flyout (which steps aside once the drag ends). Tests stop at the OS drag (Xvfb can't drop). Not verified by hand: dropping into the page under the flyout, and dragging while Orbit is in the background on macOS (an inactive window takes the first click unless it accepts the first mouse, a window-wide choice). Canvases (EZ-05) don't exist yet |
| DL-07 | Download location setting (per profile) | P1 | – | – | – |  |
| DL-08 | Remove, clear and delete downloads | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Remove from List keeps the file; Delete File moves it to the Trash/Recycle Bin (never a permanent delete; stays listed and says so when it can't); Clear all, in the Library's Downloads section, takes finished downloads off the list (files stay; the partial file of a failed one goes) and keeps running, paused, held (DL-12) and resumable ones. Missing: Clear browsing data has no "Download history" choice yet (it can call downloads.clear with the profile) |
| DL-09 | The Library (container view) | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Library container (archive lane): section list on the left with the Archive, History (AR-10) and Backups (AR-11) sections; other lanes add theirs (Media, Downloads, Canvases & Notes, Spaces, Site customizations) through the registry. Reopens to the last section; Esc/⌘W close and the previous tab comes back. Its view is made once Orbit is idle after launch, so even the first open is quick (about 70 ms at 10,000 entries; later opens 10–50 ms). Downloads lane: the Media and Downloads sections (just before Downloads, Media); right after a download, a closed Library opens on Downloads next time; their items open in a Peek over the Library (⌘/Ctrl-click: a tab) |
| DL-10 | Library → Downloads section | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Library → Downloads: everything downloaded through Orbit in the profile (running ones too, wherever saved; nothing else from the folder), newest first in day groups; a row shows a picture or kind icon, name, size or progress, site and time; search by name (every word, any case); a click previews in a Peek over the Library (PDF, images, text, audio, video; other files open in their app), ⌘/Ctrl-click opens a tab; hover buttons Show in Finder/Folder, Resume, Retry, Cancel, Keep/Discard and ⋯ for the full menu (DL-04, DL-08); rows drag out (DL-06); arrow keys and Enter; a profile switcher when there are several profiles; Clear all. Only the rows on screen are drawn |
| DL-11 | Library → Media section | P2 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Library → Media: a grid of the pictures and videos downloaded in the profile (those Orbit can show), newest first by day; video tiles play muted and looping while on screen (still with reduced motion); a click opens a larger preview in a Peek (⌘/Ctrl-click: a tab), tiles drag out as the file, right-click shows the file's menu. Right-click the Library button → Show Screenshots in Library adds the OS screenshots (macOS: the system's screenshot folder, else the Desktop; Windows: Pictures\Screenshots; Linux: Pictures/Screenshots and screenshot-named files in Pictures). Missing: in-browser captures (OT-03 doesn't exist) |
| DL-12 | Download safety | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | finished files carry the OS mark of a file from the internet (the macOS quarantine attribute; on Windows a Zone.Identifier with the page and file address, no passwords; Linux has none). Programs, installers, scripts and disk images (exe, msi, dmg, pkg, deb, rpm, AppImage, jar, apk…; Windows-only script types on Windows) wait under their partial name with Keep / Discard in the sidebar row, the Library and the flyout, through a restart too; Keep puts the file in place and marks it, Discard deletes it. Every such file is held, whatever the site, as there is no reputation service. Gap: Safe Browsing (no free reputation service to use) |
| DL-13 | Files the browser can show inline | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e | – | PDFs (the engine's viewer), pictures, plain text, audio and video open in a tab; a site that sends the file as an attachment still downloads it (DL-01); the PDF viewer's download button saves through the usual download flow (row, Library, DL-02 flight). Missing: offering Orbit as Windows' app for local .pdf files (Settings → General, P2): it needs the installer's file association and opening files passed on the command line |
| DL-14 | Downloads keyboard shortcut and menu | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Windows/Linux: Ctrl+J opens the downloads flyout at the top left, beside the sidebar (Orbit has no top toolbar): the 12 newest with live progress, Keep/Discard, Resume/Retry/Cancel and Show in Folder; a click opens a file, rows drag out (DL-06), Show All opens the Library's Downloads section; Esc, Ctrl+J again or a click outside closes it. macOS: ⌘⇧J and ⌥⌘L open the Library's Downloads section (KS-12). The command bar has a "Downloads" action |
| DL-15 | Pause, resume and retry | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Pause/Resume from the row's menu (and a Resume button on a paused row); a cut-off download shows Resume when the server sent an ETag or Last-Modified (continues with a range request), else Retry (starts again); one cut off by quitting resumes after a restart from its partial file (kept under a hidden second name while the engine shuts down). Downloads never block the tab that started them |
| DL-16 | Downloads in private windows, Little windows and Peek | P2 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e | – | Peek and Mini Window downloads go to the same list as any other. A private (in-memory) session's downloads save to disk but are in no saved list; they are listed while the session has pages and leave when its last page closes. Private windows themselves don't exist yet: tested with a profile on an in-memory session |
| DL-17 | Dock / taskbar progress | P2 | – | – | – |  |
| DL-18 | Smart renaming of downloads | OOS | ⛔ out of scope | – | – | the spec leaves it out |
